# 070-clock-generation — info

*Generated by `096` from the declarations in `070-clock-generation.md`. Do not edit this page;
edit the blueprint and run the sweep again.*

**Where the beat comes from** — phase 10.
Described by `1001`.

## What it publishes

| symbol | unit | kind | value | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `f_ref` | MHz | given | 100 MHz | the external crystal reference |
| `jit_ref` | ps | given | 0.5 ps | cycle-to-cycle jitter of the reference |
| `jit_mult` | ps | given | 3 ps | jitter one multiplier adds |
| `psrr_mult` | 1 | given | 0.02 | fraction of a supply excursion that appears as a timing shift at the multiplier's output |
| `t_lock_mult` | s | given | 0.0003 s | how long a multiplier takes to settle from cold |
| `n_ref` | 1 | given | 1 | references in the machine |
| `P_clockgen` | W | given | 4 W | all the multipliers together |
| `ratio_face` | 1 | derived | 14 | multiplier ratio for the face domain |
| `ratio_core` | 1 | derived | 12.5 | and for the core |
| `jit_total` | ps | derived | 3.04138 ps | jitter at a multiplier's output, the two sources added in quadrature since they are independent |
| `t_cycle_face` | ps | derived | 714.286 ps | the face cycle time everything in 074 is budgeted against |
| `jit_supply` | ps | derived | 0.428571 ps | timing shift caused by the supply drooping under a load step, which arrives at the worst possible moment |
| `jit_budget` | ps | derived | 3.46995 ps | what 074 must allow for altogether |
| `f_merge_gap` | 1 | derived | 1.12 | how much faster the faces run than the core, which is the question of whether the two domains can be one |

## What it consumes

| symbol | from | value | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `P_load` | `020` | 1609.28 W | power delivered to the point of load |
| `V_logic` | `029` | 0.75 V | logic and multiplier arrays |
| `dV_droop_logic` | `029` | 0.0225 V | how far the logic rail may fall during a load step, which is what sizes the decoupling in 031 |
| `f_core` | `034` | 1.25 GHz | core clock, set by the array access time in 035 |
| `f_face` | `045` | 1.4 GHz | the face clock |
| `t_powerup_max` | `033` | 0.1 s | the longest the supplies may take to reach the point where reset can be released; a person waiting for a machine notices a tenth of a second and not much less |

## What it asserts

| tag | relation | because |
|---|---|---|
| `C-070-1` | `ratio_face == floor(ratio_face)` | the face multiplier ratio must be a whole number, or the reference and the face clock have no common edge and 072's timebase cannot be derived from both |
| `C-070-2` | `jit_budget < t_cycle_face * 0.05` | jitter altogether must stay under a twentieth of a cycle, which is what 074's budget allocates to it |
| `C-070-3` | `jit_supply < jit_total` | supply-induced jitter must be smaller than the oscillator's own, or the filtered supply is not filtered. This is the term that appears exactly when the machine is busiest, so it is the one worth constraining separately |
| `C-070-4` | `n_ref == 1` | one reference. Asserted as a value, because six would drift apart and 072's shared timebase would stop being shared |
| `C-070-5` | `t_lock_mult < t_powerup_max` | the multipliers must settle inside the power-up time 033 allows |
| `C-070-6` | `P_clockgen < P_load / 100` | generating the clock must cost under a hundredth of the machine |
